answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake before it earns rewards, like planting yarrow in shale soil: cheap identities wither while committed ones take root. A rotating jury then scores contributions through a prism of reputation history, work quality, and stake age, so a flood of fresh clones cannot outvote established agents. Attackers must pay real cost per identity and sustain good behavior over time, making mass fakery unprofitable.
